theater: 泰河谷與喀裏多尼亞高地

battle.name: 羅馬入侵喀裏多尼亞
battle.theater: 泰河谷與喀裏多尼亞高地
battle.brief: 公元二〇八年春，皇帝塞維魯率約四萬人抵達不列顛，先整飭哈德良長城，再北取安東尼長城，二〇九年深入喀裏多尼亞高地，遭游擊與斷糧重創，卒於二一一年二月四日約克。卡拉卡拉隨即罷兵，羅軍退回哈德良長城。卡面這具羅馬重步兵，正是這場戰役推進與撤退時的骨幹。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 這場戰爭是羅馬帝國對喀裏多尼亞（今日蘇格蘭北部）的入侵與鎮壓，交戰地由福思河—克萊德河一線向北推入泰河谷與高地，歷時自二〇八年至二一一年。羅馬方面由皇帝塞維魯親任最高統帥，野戰軍由帝國直轄的軍團與各行省抽調的輔助兵團組成，骨幹是第二奧古斯都、第六勝利、第十九名譽凱旋等軍團的部隊，輔以騎兵隊、弓箭手、標槍手、投石手與弩炮兵，另有不列顛戰隊負責沿東岸輸送與補給。英國行省總督昆圖斯・洛利烏斯・烏爾比庫斯管轄地方行政、徵發糧秣與徵召守軍，邊境由哈德良長城沿線守軍接應，工程兵、測量員與築城人員隨軍先行開路。卡爾特一方並非單一國家，而是以卡爾特人為主、聯合梅阿泰等部族的鬆散聯盟，既無常備軍亦無中央指揮，只能臨時徵召弓手、投槍手與輕裝步兵，依托森林、沼澤、峽谷與高地堡壘作戰，以襲擾、夜襲與斷糧為主要手段，戰爭本質是帝國的野戰縱隊對一整片沒有道路的荒野。
countriesEn: This war was a Roman imperial invasion and pacification of Caledonia, the northern third of what is now Scotland, fought from 208 to 211. The theatre ran from the line of the Forth and Clyde northward into the Tay valley and the Highland glens. On the Roman side the supreme command was held in person by the emperor Septimius Severus. The field army combined legionary detachments drawn from the second Augusta, the sixth Victrix and the twentieth Valeria Victrix with auxiliary contingents supplied by the provinces, including cavalry alae, archers, javelinmen, slingers and ballista crews, while the Classis Britannica carried troops and supplies along the east coast. Q. Lollius Urbicus, governor of Britain, handled local administration, the requisition of grain and the raising of the garrison; the garrisons of Hadrian's Wall provided the line of support, and engineers, surveyors and builders marched ahead of the columns. The Caledonian side was not a state at all but a loose confederation of tribes, centred on the Caledonii north of the Forth and joined by peoples such as the Maeatae. It had no standing army and no central command, and could only levy bowmen, javelin throwers and light infantry, fighting from forests, marshes, glens and hill forts, and relying on harassment, night attacks and the cutting of supply lines rather than on any set-piece battle. In its essence the war was an imperial marching column set against an entire roadless wilderness.
people: 皇帝塞維魯是全場唯一的最高指揮者。他以六十餘歲之齡、抱病之身遠征，狄奧《羅馬史》記載他多數路程乘有篷擔架而行，直到島之北端仍留心觀察太陽運行的變化與夏日晝長的差異，說明他清楚這趟遠征的地理極限，並曾以「抵達島之盡頭」作為目標。長子卡拉卡拉於二一〇年初率一支偏師越過安東尼長城向北作懲罰性遠征，企圖以掃蕩與焚毀逼迫各部族屈服，卻在陣前遭遇反擊、險些喪命，狄奧記下皇帝當時按住劍柄對他說，你要打就給你打，但若想殺我，現在就殺。幼子蓋塔隨軍在側，未聞有獨立指揮紀錄。卡爾特方面的領袖姓名多已不可考，狄奧提到卡爾加庫斯這個名號（同一名號也見於塔西陀《阿格里科拉傳》所記的八十年代戰事），另一名在文獻中留名的首領是阿爾真托科索斯，二一〇至二一一年間的休戰交涉即以其為對話方。英國總督洛利烏斯・烏爾比庫斯負責徵召守軍、徵發糧秣與維持沿海航線，是後勤端最關鍵的人物；而在後方主持談判的塞維魯之妻朱莉婭・多米娜，同樣左右了最後的收兵。
peopleEn: The emperor Septimius Severus was the single supreme commander of the campaign. He campaigned in his sixties and in poor health, and Cassius Dio records that he was carried for most of the journey in a covered litter, and that even at the northern extremity of the island he took careful note of the changing arc of the sun and of the differing length of days in summer, which shows that he understood the geographical limit of the expedition and had set reaching the end of the island as his goal. His elder son Caracalla led a detached punitive expedition north of the Antonine Wall in early 210, trying to force the tribes to yield by sweeping and burning, and nearly met his death in a counter-attack; Dio has the emperor gripping his sword and telling him that he could have the war if he wanted it, but if he meant to kill his father he should do it there and then. The younger son Geta was present with the army, with no separate command of his own on record. The names of the Caledonian leaders are largely lost; Dio mentions Calgacus, a name that also appears in Tacitus's Agricola for the fighting of the eighties, and another leader named in the sources is Argentocoxos, the counterpart in the truce negotiations of 210 and 211. Lollius Urbicus, governor of Britain, was in charge of raising the garrison, requisitioning grain and keeping the coastal sea route open, and was the most decisive figure on the logistic side. Behind the lines, Julia Domna, wife of Severus, directed the negotiations that finally ended the campaign.
kits: 卡面這具羅馬重步兵是全軍骨幹：分段式鎧甲覆身，橢圓大盾（scutum）可覆全身，雙手持握；主兵器是加長標槍（pilum），槍桿加鐵製矛頭長約兩米，交手前先擲出壓制敵陣，再抽短劍（gladius）與匕首近身格鬥。輔助兵團補足了帝國的遠程火力：弓手、標槍手、投石手，以及弩炮（ballista）與扭力式投石機（onager）；騎兵隊（alae）負責追擊與護衛兩翼，馬匹、鞍具與繫馬繩都需自備，冬天還要餵飼大量芻料。工程裝備包括斧、鋤、繩索、絞盤、攻城塔與可拆裝的浮橋，用來在沼澤與河道上架設通道，帳幕、帳杆與炊具則按軍需清單逐日攜行。卡爾特一方沒有攻城器械，也沒有大規模的金屬鍛冶，裝備以木柄長矛、投槍、短弓、鐵刃與小型圓盾為主，另備木盾與陷阱，箭矢用得起，卻造不出可攻城的器械，戰術上完全依賴地形與行軍節奏。
kitsEn: The Roman legionary on the card is the backbone of the whole army: segmented plate armour over the body, an oval scutum large enough to cover the man and grasped with both hands, and as the main weapon the long pilum, a javelin with an iron head on a shaft some two metres long, thrown to break up the enemy formation before the legionary closed to the sword and the pugio. The auxiliary contingents supplied the empire's long-range punch: archers, javelinmen, slingers, and the ballista and the onager for heavier shots. Cavalry alae handled pursuit and the protection of both flanks, and brought their own horses, saddles and tethering lines, and in winter they also had to be fed a constant supply of fodder. Engineer equipment included axes, spades, rope, winches, siege towers and dismantlable pontoon bridges, used to open causeways across marsh and river, while tents, tent poles and cooking gear were carried according to a daily ration list. The Caledonian side owned no siege machinery and had no large-scale metalworking, and armed itself with wooden-shafted spears, javelins, short bows, iron blades and small round shields, supplemented by wooden shields and traps. They could afford arrows but never siege engines, and their method depended entirely on terrain and on the pace of the marching column.
tactics: 羅軍的推進形態是典型的工程先導、縱隊跟進。輔助兵與工程兵先在前方砍伐森林、填平沼澤、架橋修路，主力軍團以密集縱隊在狹窄通道中魚貫前行，每晚按羅軍營制挖出方形營地、掘壕立柵、按清單搭起帳幕，營地本身就是一段可守的工事。卡爾特人不敢列陣會戰，只把牛羊擋在路前引誘羅軍深入，待隊形散開、士卒脫力再行襲擊，羅軍在開闢道路時的損失遠多於正面戰鬥，狄奧甚至寫道有士卒因走不動路而被自己人殺死，以免被俘。營壘方面，羅軍冬季多宿於河谷低地，水源、燃料與糧秣最為缺乏；前進基地如泰河谷的卡爾波（Carpow）儲存軍需與攻具，恰恰成為游擊襲擊的目標。卡爾特方的戰術核心有四：夜襲營地、火燒糧草、破壞道路橋樑、封鎖峽谷谷口迫使羅軍分兵。他們也攻陷羅軍前進基地，於二一〇至二一一年間造成新據點一度淪陷，迫使羅軍分兵回援，而每一次分兵都令原本脆弱的補給線更長。
tacticsEn: The Roman advance followed the classic pattern of engineers leading and columns following. Auxiliaries and engineers felled forest, filled marsh and bridged the rivers ahead of the marching army, while the legions moved in dense columns, threading the narrow passes single file, and each night the army dug out a square camp, cut a ditch, raised a palisade and pitched its tents according to a written list, so that the camp itself was a piece of fortification. The Caledonians did not offer battle in array; they drove cattle and sheep in front of the column to draw the Romans further on, then attacked once the formation had scattered and the men were spent, so that the Roman losses in opening the route far exceeded those of any pitched fight. Dio even records that some soldiers, unable to walk any further, were killed by their own comrades rather than taken prisoner. On the march the Romans wintered mostly in the low river valleys, where water, fuel and grain were scarcest, and forward bases such as Carpow in the Tay valley, which stored the army's supplies and siege equipment, became the obvious targets of the raiders. The Caledonian method rested on four things: night attacks on camp, burning of grain, destruction of roads and bridges, and the blocking of glen mouths to force the Roman column to divide. They also overran Roman forward bases, and between 210 and 211 newly built positions fell once more, obliging the Romans to detach and recover them, and every detachment lengthened an already overstretched supply line.
data: 可查的數字都來自二手估算與古代記載，須留有餘地。塞維魯二〇八年抵英時所帶兵力，一般引述為約四萬人（Mattingly《An Imperial Possession》第123頁），另有學者依羅馬行省駐軍規模推算為四萬至五萬；同期不列顛全境羅軍駐防約四萬八千七百人，其中包含三個軍團（Breeze 2006 第42頁）。狄奧記載羅軍在戰役中損失約五萬人，現代史家認為此數明顯誇大，多半是疾病、飢餓與行軍疲勞而非戰鬥所致。狄奧另記卡爾特方面有大批降卒與俘虜，後世常引十萬至十五萬之數，但這類數字不宜當作精確統計。哈德良長城西段原本多為土牆與木柵，塞維魯此役將其改砌石造；安東尼長城則是草皮高牆，長約六十公里，沿線設十九座堡壘，西起基爾帕特里克，東訖布內斯。整場戰役自二〇八年打到二一一年二月四日塞維魯病逝於約克，前後約三年；蘇格蘭境內發現的羅馬行軍營地密度，是全歐最高的，而安東尼長城時期獲證長期設防的堡壘只有克拉蒙德與卡爾波兩處。
dataEn: Every usable figure comes either from a modern estimate or from an ancient text, and all of them need to be treated with care. The force Severus brought to Britain in 208 is usually given as about forty thousand men (Mattingly, An Imperial Possession, p. 123), while other scholars, reasoning from the size of the provincial garrison, put the total at forty to fifty thousand; the whole Roman force then stationed in Britain numbered about forty-eight thousand seven hundred men, including three legions (Breeze 2006, p. 42). Dio records about fifty thousand Roman dead in the campaign, a figure modern historians regard as plainly exaggerated, most of the loss having come from disease, hunger and exhaustion on the march rather than from fighting. Dio also notes large numbers of Caledonian prisoners and surrendered, a claim often quoted as a hundred or a hundred and fifty thousand, but such numbers should not be treated as precise statistics. The western section of Hadrian's Wall had been largely turf and timber; Severus rebuilt it in stone during this campaign. The Antonine Wall was a turf rampart about sixty kilometres long with nineteen forts along it, running from Old Kilpatrick in the west to Bo'ness in the east. The campaign ran from 208 until the death of Severus at York on 4 February 211, something like three years in all. The density of Roman marching camps found in Scotland is the highest anywhere in Europe, and only two forts, Cramond and Carpow, are certainly known to have been held permanently during the Antonine occupation.
cause: 直接原因是北方的襲擊越來越頻繁。公元一九五年，不列顛總督克勞狄烏斯・阿爾比努斯帶領大部分英國軍團投向高盧，參與對塞維魯的反叛；塞維魯在路迪古努斯擊敗他之後把軍團調回原防，但這些部隊在內戰中損失慘重，北方前線的駐軍密度隨之下降，哈德良長城沿線出現空缺。卡爾特人趁機加強各部族之間的協作，能投入更多兵力南下掠奪，而羅方守軍既不足，也不熟悉高地與森林戰術。塞維魯自稱是被梅阿泰一類部族的挑釁所逼，不得不應戰；從帝國政治看，他在一九三至一九七年的內戰之後甫掌朝綱、元氣未復，需要一場勝利來壓服剛剛平定的東方與內陸的挑戰者，為接班安排鋪路，同時把不列顛北境的防線從土牆改造成石牆，恢復帝國疆界的完整與威懾。
causeEn: The immediate cause was a sharp rise in raids from the north. In 195 the governor of Britain, Clodius Albinus, took most of the British legions away to Gaul in his revolt against Severus. After defeating him at Lugdunum, Severus sent the legions back to their posts, but they had been badly mauled in the civil war, the density of the northern frontier had fallen with them, and gaps opened along Hadrian's Wall. The Caledonians took advantage of this to cooperate more closely among their tribes and to bring larger forces to their raids, while the Roman defenders were too few and knew little of fighting in hill and forest country. Severus claimed that he was forced into the war by the provocations of tribes such as the Maeatae. In imperial terms, he had taken the throne only after the civil wars of 193 to 197 and was not yet secure; he needed a victory to overawe challengers in the east and the interior who had only just been subdued, to make secure the succession arrangements, and to rebuild the northern frontier of Britain from a turf line into a stone one, restoring the empire's frontier to a full and menacing state.
impact: 這場戰役的結果不是征服，而是邊界。哈德良長城西段全線改砌石材，成為羅馬帝國在北方最耐用的防線；安東尼長城也經過重修並短暫駐軍。安東尼長城時期，蘇格蘭境內確認長期設防的堡壘只有兩處：福思灣畔的克拉蒙德與泰河谷的卡爾波，兩處都屬塞維魯時期的駐軍，撤軍後同樣被放棄。卡爾特各部族遭到重創，掠奪與焚毀造成的損失要靠多年才恢復過來，其再度集結大規模南下的能力被明顯削弱，這也是羅馬此後長久不曾再深入喀裏多尼亞的原因之一。帝國自身的負擔同樣真實：北方戰役加重了塞維魯的病情，他在二一一年二月四日病逝於約克；繼位的卡拉卡拉隨即殺死弟弟蓋塔，帝國立刻陷入內廷的緊張，此後再無力向北用兵。此外，羅馬與高地部族之間的往來也帶來實物交換，錢幣、陶器與工藝品在北境出現，說明雙方之間並非只有兵戎，戰爭同樣是一條打開北方的通道。
impactEn: The result of this campaign was not a conquest but a frontier. The western stretch of Hadrian's Wall was rebuilt entirely in stone and became the most durable defensive line the empire held in the north, and the Antonine Wall was likewise repaired and briefly garrisoned. During the Antonine occupation only two forts in Scotland are certainly known to have been held permanently: Cramond on the Firth of Forth and Carpow in the Tay valley, both Severan-period stations that were abandoned again when the troops withdrew. The Caledonian tribes were badly hit, and the losses from raiding and burning would take years to repair; their ability to raise large forces for a southern raid was clearly diminished, which is one reason Rome never again drove deep into Caledonia. The cost to the empire was equally real: the northern campaign aggravated Severus's illness and he died at York on 4 February 211, and the successor Caracalla promptly had his brother Geta killed, throwing the court into immediate tension; the empire had no further strength to spend in the north. Exchange of goods also continued: coins, pottery and worked objects from Roman workshops appear in the north, which shows that the war was not only a war, and that it opened a channel into the far north as well.
result: 二一〇年，塞維魯在一次北進之後病勢加重，退回約克休養，至二一一年二月四日病逝，年六十餘。卡拉卡拉接手後不願再打這場沒有收官的戰爭，下令全軍南撤，放棄安東尼長城一線的據點，把邊界退回哈德良長城；考古與文獻都顯示，蘇格蘭境內的塞維魯時期營地在二一二年至二一三年之間被大批放棄。卡爾特人未被打服，但以放棄部分土地、停止南掠為條件換得停戰，狄奧記載羅軍退回「友好之地」後才接受這樣的結果，並提到北境修築了一道用來分隔雙方的土牆，即後世所稱的「塞維魯之牆」，其具體位置至今仍有爭議，一般推測與福思河一線的草皮防線重合。總結而言：羅軍在戰術上深入到前人未至的高地，在戰略上則全數退回，喀裏多尼亞未被征服，羅馬此後不再企圖重蹈這場戰役的覆轍，雙方的邊界從此定型在哈德良長城。
resultEn: In 210 Severus's condition worsened after one of his northern drives, and he withdrew to York to rest, where he died on 4 February 211 in his sixties. Caracalla, taking over, had no wish to fight on in a war that would not end; he ordered the whole army south, abandoned the positions on the Antonine Wall line and moved the frontier back to Hadrian's Wall. Archaeology and the written sources alike show that the Severan camps in Scotland were largely abandoned between 212 and 213. The Caledonians were not beaten, but they obtained a truce on condition that they gave up part of their territory and stopped raiding south, and Dio records that the Romans accepted this only after returning to the friendly part of the island. He also mentions that a wall of turf was built in the north to divide the two sides, the wall later called the Wall of Severus; its precise location remains disputed, and it is generally supposed to coincide with the turf line on the Forth. In sum: the Romans advanced tactically into highlands no Roman had reached before, and withdrew strategically in full. Caledonia was not conquered, Rome never again attempted what this campaign had attempted, and the boundary between the two sides was fixed for good at Hadrian's Wall.
